title: Coming alongside a quay and leaving with springs
h1: Coming alongside and leaving with springs
lead: Fuel docks, pontoons, quiet town quays and rafting up all mean berthing alongside. Here is how to prepare, come in under control and spring off again.
description: How to come alongside a quay or pontoon: fenders, lines and springs, approach angle, wind and prop walk, the first line ashore, springing off and rafting up.
summary: Set fenders at the height of the quay, lines and springs ready, and brief the crew to step off, never jump.
Approach slowly at 20 to 30 degrees: steeper with the wind off the quay, shallower with it blowing on.
Get a midships spring led aft ashore first, then hold the boat in with gentle ahead power.
To leave a tight berth, motor against a slip spring to swing the stern or bow out first.
